name: Vagal Regulation and Social Engagement System

mechanism_chain.description: Environmental features that signal safety to the autonomic nervous system: low ambient noise (LAeq < 55 dBA), adequate lighting for facial recognition (>200 lux at face level), visual sightlines, absence of concealed approach vectors, nature elements.

data.finding: Ambient noise LAeq > 60 dBA reduces RSA by ~15%
data.paradigm: Cardiac autonomic measurement during noise exposure
data.effect: Noise shifts autonomic state away from social engagement

data.finding: Nature views increase RSA ~8-12% with exposure ≥ 10 minutes
data.source: Park et al. (2010); Li et al. (2011)
data.effect: Nature elements support vagal safety state

justification.backing: Porges' neuroception construct holds that the autonomic nervous system detects environmental safety/threat cues below conscious awareness. The specific architectural features (noise, lighting, sightlines) have empirically demonstrated effects on RSA.
justification.qualifier: The neuroception pathway is theoretically grounded; direct measurement of the neural pathway from environmental features to nucleus ambiguus in architectural contexts is absent.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if RSA changes are mediated by conscious appraisal rather than automatic neuroception; cognitive interpretation may dominate automatic detection.

mechanism_chain.description: Safety signals promote ventral vagal complex (nucleus ambiguus) activation, indexed by increased RSA/RMSSD. Ventral vagal state supports social engagement: facial expression, vocalization, listening attuned to human voice frequencies.
mechanism_chain.note: CONSTRAINT: phylogenetic ordering (dorsal → sympathetic → ventral) is THEORETICAL_DEFAULT. Functional RSA modulation is empirically supported.

data.finding: RSA/RMSSD reliably indexes vagal regulation; normative resting RSA ~40-60 ms (ln-RMSSD 3.5-4.0) in young healthy adults
data.effect: RSA as index of vagal state

data.finding: Phylogenetic ordering (dorsal → sympathetic → ventral) contested by Grossman (2023)

justification.backing: The Social Engagement System (Porges 2007) comprises neural regulation of facial expression, vocalization, and listening. The functional RSA data are well-supported; the broader phylogenetic claims carry THEORETICAL_DEFAULT.
justification.qualifier: Porges acknowledged the constraint: phylogenetic ordering is contested but functional RSA modulation is independently supported.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if RSA is not a valid index of vagal regulation; alternative cardiac measures might be required.

competing_accounts.resolution: Panel limited Porges' contribution to empirically supported RSA modulation, flagged phylogenetic claims as THEORETICAL_DEFAULT

mechanism_chain.description: High RSA state associated with prosocial behavior, emotional regulation, and social approach. Reduced RSA associated with social withdrawal, defensive behavior.

data.finding: High RSA predicts prosocial behavior, emotional regulation, and social approach; low RSA predicts withdrawal and defensive behavior
data.paradigm: Behavioral correlates of cardiac vagal tone

justification.backing: The RSA-behavior link is well-established in the developmental and clinical literature. High vagal tone supports the physiological platform for social engagement.
justification.qualifier: The association is correlational; causality is inferred from the proposed mechanism. Experimental manipulation of architectural features with RSA outcomes would strengthen the claim.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if RSA-behavior associations are confounded by individual differences (personality, anxiety) that are not architecturally modifiable.

vagal_regulation.description: Normative resting RSA in seated healthy young adult. Values below ln-RMSSD 3.4 indicate shift away from ventral vagal social engagement.

acoustic_environment.effect: RSA reduction ~15% above LAeq 60 dBA in sustained exposure

nature_view_quality.effect: RSA increase ~8–12% with nature view exposure ≥ 10 minutes
nature_view_quality.source: Park et al. 2010; Li et al. 2011
nature_view_quality.note: Partial overlap with VIEW1 Channel 5. See amygdala partial-out protocol.

interpersonal_distance.rsa_increase: 8–12% above solitary baseline when in presence of non-threatening familiar other at conversational distance

visual_sightline_depth.note: Ability to see approaching others from ≥6 m

concealed_approach_absence.description: No blind corners or concealed doorways within 3 m of social seating

phylogenetic_ordering_flag.note: The dorsal vagal → sympathetic → ventral vagal evolutionary sequence (Porges 1995) is contested by Grossman (2023). The functional RSA modulation data are supported independently of the phylogenetic claim.

hpa_axis_activation.description: NM_VAGAL_REGULATION_001 shares amygdala pathway with VIEW1 Ch5 and PROXEMIC_PE_ARCH_001. IC2 contribution = max(individual_template_amygdala_contributions) + 0.15 × sum(remaining). See Debate 5 consensus.

ie_dpt_interaction: T_IE_004 (Autonomic Readiness × Social Context) — vagal state gates social engagement capacity

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — ventral vagal state is the IC2 'social rest' mode. Shift to sympathetic mobilization incurs IC2 cost. Sustained low-RSA environments (noisy, poorly lit, threatening) accumulate body-budget debt via the same HPA pathway as T6/T7 but through autonomic rather than cortisol mediation.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — control over noise (operable windows, acoustic shielding), lighting (task lighting), and social approach (choice of seating location) all enhance neuroception of safety and thereby support ventral vagal state.
